textRuns.value: Global emissions in 1750 were 9.4 Mt, almost all of it British coal, so the United Kingdom's 100% share reflects a very small absolute base rather than a large one. The same chart at 1900 shows global emissions of 1,952 Mt with the United Kingdom still above 25%.

The year filter sets 2021 for the scatter and the matrix but means different things to each measure. Current emissions are for that year alone. Cumulative emissions are the running total from 1750 up to it. The United Kingdom is the extreme case at 0.21: it emits a fifth of its historical share, the lowest ratio of the twenty largest historical emitters.
